newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, choice issue seen gaining.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, choice issue seen gaining.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Wednesday in modest trade, which was expected to slow down further by the end of this week save for a few choice issues.
Traders outlined the current market favourite -- brewery Karlovacka Pivovara -- chocolate maker Kras and hotelier Laguna as likely to gain on the back of strong investor interest.
"I expect Kras and Laguna to rise mildly and the rest of the market to stabilise," said Domagoj Grabovac of Fima brokerage.

"The situation with these two is typical for a period just before the annual meeting. By the same token, Zagrebacka Banka and (drugs firm) Pliva are already receeding after a very steep rise," he said.
Six of 13 stocks rose, five fell and two ended flat on Wednesday. Buyers went for a handful of firms and bought them in quantities topping 1,000 shares, while the others were more or less dormant.
Traders noted a growing demand for industrial stocks -- Zagreb's tobacco factory TDZ, Nasicecement and coffee roaster Franck -- which were not offered for sale.
Volume shrank slightly to 8,461 units while turnover rose to 7.7 from 4.8 million kuna.
The day's biggest gainer Karlovacka added 20 kuna or 3.51 percent to 590 kuna on volume of 301 shares. Denis Fuduric of IB Austria saw it rising another 10 kuna in the near term.
"I think it will hit resistance at 600 or 601 kuna," he said of the Croatian subsidiary of Chile's Compania Cervecerias Unidas SA, which posted excellent 1996 results.
Fully-listed Varazdinska Banka's first issue led decliners, losing 10 kuna or 4.54 percent to 210 kuna with 520 units sold.
Laguna, selling 1,726 shares, was the most active issue. It rose eight kuna or 0.53 percent to 1,509 kuna.
Blue chip Zagrebacka Banka ordinaries gained 40 kuna or 2.08 percent to 1,960 kuna on volume of 1,318, making them the second most actively traded stock.
Its preferred E-series rose 45 kuna or 3.16 percent to 1,470 kuna on volume of 758, with a prospect of firming.
Pliva lost one kuna to 479 with 119 shares sold and was seen as dipping to around 450-460.
Kras, with 1,240 shares sold, climbed five kuna to 435 -- the level at which it could stabilise shortly, traders said.
But they saw room for further decline of another food stock Podravka, which has fallen steadily over the past week to end two kuna lower at 252 on Wednesday.
Privatisation candidate Koncar electrical group slid to 1,245 kuna from 1,260 after shooting up when plans to float 31 percent of its shares in about a year were announced.
